title: Backlog.md migration mints ids outside the id allocator
description: Found by the round 1 review of opum-ai/quest-cli#646 (QCLI-495, finding 8). The Backlog.md migration mints task and milestone ids itself, from its own worktree alone, with no refs scan, no worktree scan, no ledger and no lock: src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts around :314-324 (dotted-subtask ids), :477-485 (the task id from a prefix and highest+index+1) and :611-623 (M-N milestone ids). QCLI-495 put every create command through src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts and says in its summary, the changelog and the shipped guide that migration is NOT covered. Pre-existing, not a regression. Filed only: not started, and the allocator was deliberately not extended here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `migration backlog apply` allocates every task and milestone id it mints through the shared allocator, or a recorded decision says why it need not
Two worktrees of one repository that each run a migration apply before either commits do not mint the same id, proved both ways

plan: 1. Read the migration id minting: src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts computes task ids from a worktree-local highest+index+1, dotted subtasks from a local mintCounter, and milestone ids from a local M-<n> scan -- no lock, ledger or worktree scan.

2. Add a block API to the shared allocator (peekIdBlock for a reservation a caller must not make, reserveIdBlock for one it must), both reading the same lock/ledger/worktree sources the single-id path uses.

3. Thread an optional BacklogIdAllocation (git, worktree root, common-dir resolver) into BacklogImportService: preview peeks, apply reserves and refuses with migration_id_block_moved if the reserved block differs from the approved one; milestones reserve at apply (they never enter the digest); --preserve-source-ids mints its dotted replacements in the source family marker.
4. Wire the allocator from composition and the four migration CLI call sites; keep the no-allocator path (raw QUEST_TASK_STORE, direct-service fixtures) on the old arithmetic.

5. Test in test/qcli520-migration-allocator.test.ts with real worktrees: the control computes the pre-fix rule and shows both worktrees minting T-1/T-2; the fix migrates in both before either commits and asserts disjoint task ids (T-1/T-2 vs T-3/T-4) and milestone ids (M-1 vs M-2), plus the durable ledger entries.
6. Mutation control: bypass the allocator and confirm the test goes red, then restore.
7. Update the shipped guide and the Unreleased changelog, which both said the migration is not covered.
8. bun run check, commit on fix/QCLI-520-migration-id-allocator, push, open the PR, report the head SHA.
implementationNotes: Evidence, 2026-10-21. Allocation goes through the shared allocator in three places: positional task ids (peek at preview, reserve at apply), --preserve-source-ids dotted replacements (allocated in the source family marker, e.g. ODOC-), and milestone ids (reserved at apply; they never enter the approved digest, so reserving immediately is safe). Apply peeks first so a stale digest reserves nothing, then reserves and compares; a mismatch is migration_id_block_moved (exit 6, message asks for a re-preview) rather than a silent renumber. TEST, real git worktrees: the control computes the pre-fix rule in two fresh worktrees and shows both minting T-1/T-2; the fix migrates in both before either commits and asserts T-1/T-2 vs T-3/T-4 and M-1 vs M-2, task id sets disjoint, and the ledger holds the first block after apply 1 (T-1, T-2, M-1) and the second after apply 2 (T-3, T-4, M-2) -- the first block is pruned once its records are visible in a worktree, which is the ledger own rule. MUTATION CONTROL for AC2: forcing idBlock to return [] (allocator bypassed, pre-fix arithmetic) turns the test red; restored it passes. bun run check: typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check and 1267 unit tests all pass; the local test:mod arm fails on six pre-existing board.test.tsx typecheck errors in the mod stage (environmental, documented elsewhere), no error in src/.
finalSummary: Delivered on fix/QCLI-520-migration-id-allocator. migration backlog apply now mints every task and milestone id it allocates through the shared allocator (QCLI-495 common-dir lock, reservation ledger and worktree scan): the positional task block is peeked at preview and reserved at apply, --preserve-source-ids mints its dotted replacements in the source family marker, and milestone ids are reserved at apply. A reservation that does not reproduce the block the approved digest describes is refused as migration_id_block_moved with a re-preview instruction, never silently renumbered. Callers with no Git repository behind their store keep the old arithmetic. Evidence, proved both ways with real worktrees: the control computes the pre-fix rule and shows two fresh worktrees both minting T-1/T-2; the allocator path migrates in both before either commits and yields T-1/T-2 vs T-3/T-4 with milestones M-1 vs M-2, disjoint, and the durable ledger entries read between the applies. Mutation control: bypassing the allocator turns the test red; restored it passes. Migration suites 58/58 and QCLI-495 allocator suites pass; bun run check green through typecheck, lint, format, layer and 1267 unit tests (the local test:mod arm carries its documented pre-existing board.test.tsx failures, none in src/).
